summary: Eventive raxu/raxiwi belong to Preterit Intransitive; raxiwo/raxiwe and feminine raxuto with kle/kla express a mounted state under Part act. Similar shapes require contextual checking.
I marks mounts with ʕal and boats with b-. III adds a causee, as a noun or suffix; PrS 30/16 contrasts ʕal i kačke with l ruḥa.
New boxes relative to rxw: I Imperativ, III Infectum and III Imperativ. Related rwx already has examples in these boxes, so no language-wide absence is claimed.

Lookup of rwx confirms rawəx/rowəx, rawixi and rawixo; exclude rawxi at 94/351–352 from rxw additions. Retain existing entry boundaries. Lookup of sym confirms the mounting-plus-intercourse sequence in sense 8.
PrS 1/38, 49/67 and 51/10 match inherited examples cited by page/line references. The III example at 49/67 legitimately includes an independent I clause; no whole-example move is justified.
Should rxw and rwx be cross-referenced or consolidated? Verify the inherited rwġ pointer.
Is Rxawu at PrS 85/28 I Imperativ addressing faroše, or a reduced III Imperativ? The bare form and following I clause favour I provisionally; German cannot decide.
Confirm reduced III Arxu at PrS 65/59 against Arxewulla at 64/64; both have overt causees.
Supply complete aligned German for PrS 80/62, 64 and 67; their translations omit the target or concern other events and are not quoted.
Are the bare human-mounting clauses at PrS 28/30, 31/42 and 77/66 conventionally sexual without sym/nyk? The accepted subsense is grounded in the explicit cases.
Conveyance extends to steamer (b-), raft, carpet and bird. Human opponents can be literal supports; a human complement alone does not establish sexual purpose.
Existing setzen includes seating people on a log used as a raft.
